headline: Arteta warns Dowman as Arsenal, Liverpool build to Anfield
paragraphs: Arsenal's best-corroborated story today is also its most settled: after a red card at Fleetwood, Max Dowman lost his appeal against the dismissal, and manager Mikel Arteta told the 16-year-old 'this is not Disneyland,' insisting he'll be held to the same standards as the rest of the squad. BBC Sport, Sky Sports and the Guardian all carried the remarks independently — a genuine three-newsroom confirmation, not a recycled wire story. The comments arrive days before Arsenal's trip to Liverpool.

That Liverpool trip is the weekend's marquee fixture among these six clubs: Sunday's match, previewed separately by Opta, the Guardian and Sky Sports, is framed as a test of whether Liverpool can be considered genuine title contenders — Sky's Paul Merson argues a win over Arsenal is a prerequisite. Separately, reports on Trent Alexander-Arnold's future conflict: BBC's gossip column said on October 24 that Liverpool have no plan to bring him back, while Transfermarkt reported on October 30 that Liverpool have been approached about his return. Neither is confirmed.

Elsewhere, Bayern's Harry Kane plays his first match since winning the Ballon d'Or in Saturday's Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund, per Opta's preview; separately, Kane told FourFourTwo a potential knighthood would feel 'weird.' On the move front, FourFourTwo reports Liverpool and Barcelona are in talks over the future of loanee Ronald Araujo — a single-source report, not confirmed by either club.
